newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-US West Coast diesel rises on supply pinch. [CORRECTED 09:42 02/8]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-US West Coast diesel rises on supply pinch. [CORRECTED 09:42 02/8]

text.p: Diesel fuel prices on the U.S. West Coast jumped nearly 11 percent this week, as refiners scrambled to replenish inventories ahead of harvest season demand from farmers, traders and state officials said Friday.
CARB gasoline prices also advanced at a slightly lower rate, traders said.

The spot price of CARB diesel, reflecting what dealers charge at the pipeline, rose seven cents a gallon to 65 cents since Tuesday afternoon, when the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported West Coast supplies fell by 313,000 barrels the prior week.
At the same time, demand shot up as farmers began building up supplies needed to fuel equipment during the upcoming harvest season.
"Diesel's pretty tight right now, with agricultural demand underway and inventories lower," said a refinery trader.
Some traders said Atlantic Richfield Co., a main supplier of West Coast diesel, was short fuel at its truck shipping terminals. "ARCO is running out in certain locations," a trader said.
An ARCO official said supply was adequate at his company's terminals, but the market had less fuel overall.

Inventories fell to 12 million barrels (corrects from 2.2 million) for the week ended July 25, after a month of heavy exporting. About one million barrels of fuel left the region because prices dipped to a paltry 53 cents in early July, traders said.
Refiners are ramping up production to make up for the shortfall. CARB diesel production has risen about 14 percent to 181,000 barrels per day, according to the California Energy Commission (CEC).
"With inventories at that level, (traders) are probably looking to capitalize on the increased price," said a spokeswoman for the CEC.
CARB gasoline prices meanwhile rose 10 percent on the week, in the wake of a 1.4 million-barrel drop in gasoline the week before.
The spot price of CARB unleaded gasoline stood at 71 cents a gallon, or seven cents above Monday's level.
